popCulture.title: Iliad
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Homer names Portheus (Porthaon) as father of the horseman Oeneus — the Aetolian trunk from which Diomedes traces his Calydonian blood on the Trojan plain.

popCulture.title: Porthaon
popCulture.description: King in Aetolia, father of Oeneus, Agrius, Melas, and their sisters — the stem of the Calydonian boar-hunt house.

popCulture.title: Oeneus
popCulture.description: Porthaon's son — king of Calydon, father of Meleager and (by Periboea) Tydeus, the hinge of Aetolian heroic myth.

popCulture.title: Bibliotheca
popCulture.creator: Apollodorus
popCulture.description: Apollodorus sets Porthaon son of Agenor over the Aetolian line — the genealogical root of the Calydonian and Tydeid heroes.
